condition.reason: The pooling kernels only accept 1-D (b,h,n) tensors and sum along the last axis, so they can never express the paper's 2-D sumpool over the softmax matrix; the code instead pools the already-reduced column-mean vector `vertical = qk.mean(-2)`.

The code always passes `vertical` as the second argument (true distribution) to square_root_js_divergence, but `vertical` is not the paper's sumpool(softmax(Q̂Kᵀ/√d)) block sum, so the true-distribution operand is replaced on every call.

Whenever the JSD comparison runs, the code uses the tau threshold to rewrite budgets and continue vertical/slash indexing instead of returning a pattern as Algorithm 2 describes, so the divergence appears on every execution of this path.

The code always computes avg_qk from last_q.mean(1) (a single mean vector) times pooled K, producing a 1×num_blocks distribution instead of the paper's pool(Q̂)·pool(K) block-level num_blocks×num_blocks distribution, regardless of inputs.

The code never normalizes the estimated attention map by its sum before flattening/thresholding, so the paper-code mismatch applies on every call to get_active_blocks/score_cover_idx regardless of input values.
The paper's threshold γ is compared against a raw cumulative sum, while the code compares against γ*num_blocks, so the two diverge whenever γ differs from γ*num_blocks (i.e., num_blocks != 1).

The union of query-aware prefix indices with vertical/slash indices always makes S differ from pure Ia[1:K] whenever get_active_blocks/transform_veritcal_slash_idx run, independent of specific input values.
